analyst.summary: CG Power had an excellent FY26 - revenue and profit both grew strongly and the order book hit a record high - and the balance sheet remains debt-free with very high returns on capital. But the market has already priced in years of continued strong growth: the stock trades near its most expensive level ever, well above global peers such as ABB and Siemens India, and even optimistic broker forecasts (assuming roughly 30% earnings growth for three more years) only justify a modest further gain from here, while at least one major broker sees roughly 30% downside if India's transmission-equipment investment cycle slows after FY27 as currently planned. Margins in the company's motors business have also weakened this year, and a new chip-manufacturing venture is still a small drag on quarterly profit while it scales up. We are not questioning CG Power's business quality - we are flagging that the price leaves very little room for anything to go wrong.
